articleTitle: Creation and Analysis of the Interval 3D Model with the Constrained Dix Inversion Method from the RMS Velocity
abstract: Velocity models are needed in the process of making 3D earth models. The interval velocity model is more representative of the actual geological condition compared to the RMS (Root Mean Square) velocity model for the reason that at the interval velocity, the ray undergoes a ray bending that satisfies Snell's law, on the contrary at the RMS velocity when the ray crosses the two layers of different density then the ray is transmitted. The geological information shows that in the research area contained reef carbonate, causing a high lateral velocity variation due to the ray bending when passing through the layer boundaries. In this research, an interval velocity model analysis of the RMS velocity model was carried out using the constrained dix inversion method. The data used include seismic data in the form of CDP (Common Depth Point) gather and RMS velocity, and well data. The result shows that the interval velocity model has a better actual geological model compared to the RMS velocity model. This is indicated by the flat depth gathers, semblance which coincides with zero residual moveout axis, and the correlation between the depth image produced by the markers (well seismic tie).

articleTitle: Inspection of Soldering Anomalies on Surface Mount Devices Using Image Processing & ANN
abstract: The quality of production in a company is a major guarantee. It needed a human resources, assistance company to control the product quality. However, human errors causing product failures are still found in many cases. Some disadvantages of using human power for the inspection process are fatigued in the eye when carrying out inspections using manual equipment such as magnifying glasses and microscopes. So in this study a system was designed to detect and identify anomalies on the soldering of ICSOIC on surface mount devices using image processing and neural networks. To separate the soldering colour from the SOIC IC, the HSL method is used while the identification of the type of anomaly in the SOIC IC used a backpropagation neural network. From the results of the system testing carried out, the success rate reached 92.72% from 11 trials.

articleTitle: Pixel-based Remote Sensing Data Processing for Estimating Rubber Plantations Productivity
abstract: Rubber plants are one of the plantation commodities that have an important role in Indonesia's economic life. Indonesia is a country with the largest rubber plantation in the world. A fast and accurate method is needed that can be used to obtain information about rubber plantation areas, one of them is to use remote sensing data. This research aims to test the results of production estimates carried out with remote sensing data with production data measured in the field. The research method used in this study is the remote sensing method and statistical data analysis using regression correlation. This research uses ASTER imagery in the visible channel and Near IR. The result of the correlation between the value of the SAVI vegetation transformation index and the width of the canopy shows that the two variables are related to each other. This is indicated by the magnitude of the value of R2 on the correlation results of these two variables at 0.709. Judging from the correlation model above, the relationship between the width of the canopy cover and the stem volume shows a very strong relationship, judging from the value of R2 which reaches up to the value of 0.816. Production of rubber plants can be seen from field data related to stem volume that has been obtained from field measurements. The level of accuracy of the study is determined using standard error (SE). This standard error (SE) value is applied to the transformations used, which is 0.7118. The SE value was obtained through a model accuracy test between the canopy and stem volume.

articleTitle: Intelligent Cuckoo Search Algorithm of Skyhook Controller for Semi-Active Suspension using MR Damper
abstract: This paper introduces the use of Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA) to tune the Skyhook controller for semi-active suspension system in furtherance of increasing and enhancing the ride comfort and vehicle stability. In the meantime, the intelligent approach with Skyhook-CSA is compared with uncontrolled passive system. The performance of the Skyhook controller is optimized by CSA, respectively. The mean square error (MSE) of the system is set as an objective function for the optimization process of the proposed controller. The performance of the Skyhook-CSA controller is compared with the passive system in terms of sprung acceleration, sprung displacement and unsprung displacement. The random road profile with 2.6 Hz frequency is set as the disturbance of the system. The simulation results reflect that the controller offers a significant improvement in ride comfort and vehicle stability by 15.47% of MSE.

articleTitle: Voice Recognition Using K-Means Clustering Based on Hidden Markov Model
abstract: Ortolan Bunting bird has various song-types. For time being, there are not so many systems which automatically cluster the song-type of Ortolan Bunting bird. Speech recognition is one example of technology development in the 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Century which uses voice as the input. This research builds an automatic system to cluster the song-type of Ortolan Bunting bird automatically using K-means clustering algorithm based on Hidden Markov Models (HMM). Commonly, HMM is used on signal processing and for speech and speaker recognition on human voice. This research uses 5 song-types of bird, and every song-type is represented by 100 songs. The data will be the clustering using K-means based HMM with 3 feature extractions and the result validation employs index stability computation. The clustering parameter groups the data into 5 clusters with dissimilarity value of 8.2 %. It means that for several times of experiments there are 8.2 % data clustered into different group and 91.8% of cluster members which always gather in the same cluster. The highest similarity level was obtained using Greenwood function cepstral coefficients delta-acceleration (GFCC_D_A) feature with 36 parameters.

articleTitle: The Suitability of the Location of Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) at BP Batam Hospital
abstract: The location of the new WWTP placement at BP Batam Hospital considers several factors that are used as parameters to determine the location of the WWTP. This study uses an overlay analysis with scoring method where the scoring process is carried out in each classification by giving the appropriate weights and values by classifying each parameter. The results obtained are in the form of a WWTP land suitability map with a land area of 0.16 Ha with a water capacity of 100 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/ day. For the processing of wastewater, the location of land suitability in the BP Batam Hospital area can be categorized as a very suitable area This is the result of slope for IPAL locations with specifications of 16-25% as flat areas which are of good density in the drainage of waste with a piping system.

articleTitle: Stability Study Of High-Speed Passenger Ship: A Case Study Of KMP Marine Hawk II
abstract: KMP Marine Hawk II is one of the highspeed craft that operates in Riau Archipelago. It carries the passenger as well as cargo in breakbulk within the archipelago area. This study aims to determine the technical stability calculation of KMP Marine Hawk II using numerical computation with Maxsurf software IMO Criteria requires GZ Max is 15 deg. In the departure full load condition, the GZ max value is 37.3 deg. In the navigation on full load GZ max value is 32.7 deg. While in the arrival full load is 25.5 deg with lightship condition 29.1 deg. All of those GZ numbers are satisfying the criteria from IMO HSC 2000 Annex 8 Mono Hull. However, the ship crew should consider the passenger-cargo stowage to maintain those GZ criteria.

articleTitle: A Control Strategy to Estimate the Robot Position Of Barelang-FC Striker
abstract: This paper presents a control strategy to move its body to the ball position before kick the ball for the humanoid robot soccer called Barelang-FC. This strategy was dedicated for the striker of Barelang-FC. The control strategy involved the robot structure and the position of camera vision. To overcome this strategy, at the first robot calculated the actual distance from robot to the ball and distinguished the opponent's goal. After getting the actual distance of the ball and the heading of the opponent's goal, a PID controller was chosen to maintain the stability of walking. To make sure the control strategy worked on the robot, a real-time application has been done on the Barelang-FC striker. The experimental results show that robot afford to move towards the ball before kicking the ball at the opponent's goal in the proper position.

articleTitle: Spatial Characteristics of Oceanography Conditions and The Relationship of Pelagic Fish
abstract: West Sumatra and its surrounding waters get a significant influence from the Indian Ocean water mass that undergoes changes both in oceanography conditions and the level of primary productivity in them. This study aims to determine the oceanography characteristics of the waters as well as their relation to pelagic fish density in the Republic of Indonesia National Fisheries Management Area (WPP-NRI). while other parameter data is obtained in situ from BPRL through CTD assistance. The highest pelagic fish density is in the area of West Sumatra Province with a range of 313.3-391.6 mg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with the highest sea surface temperature composition which is 29.7°C -30.40°C. It was noted that the area also had the highest interpretation of the value of chlorophyll-a as well as the lowest salinity value around 31.03 PSU -31.83 PSU. Pelagic fish catches in this study occurred in the transition season II.

articleTitle: Flow Simulation Analisys of Modified Lower Hose Radiator
abstract: The cooling system on the engine having a function to prevent excess heat, but also has a negative impact on the ability of the engine to produce fuel power. One way to utilize heat energy of cooling water on internal combustion engine is using a thermoelectric generator (TEG). The TEG is placed between the upper hose radiator and the lower hose radiator to utilize heat and cold sources from cooling water of the engine. In order for TEG to be placed properly, we modified the upper hose and lower hose radiator. Due to the extreme modification of the lower hose radiator, the effectiveness of the cooling water flow needs to be known. The purpose of this study was to determine the distribution of pressure from the cooling water through a lower hose radiator that has been modified. The study was conducted in a simulation using Solidwork software. The research show that the use of a modified radiator hose does not significantly reduce the pressure of fluid flow in the downstream area. The pressure drop found was only 3 kPa. However, in the hose area where the TEG is installed there is a high pressure drop. Pressure drop in this area is 5 kPa.

articleTitle: Intelligent Optimization of Force Tracking Parameters for MR Damper Modelling using Firefly Algorithm
abstract: Magnetorheological (MR) damper system is commonly used to replace the conventional damper in the suspension system due to its low power consumption, fast time response and simple structure. Since inner loop controller is very important in defining the amount of current supplied to the MR damper system, many existing controllers are found not well-structured in terms of calculating the optimum value of the controller parameter. Poor control design using the conventional method will cause the output current obtained for the MR damper to be unpredictable. To overcome this problem, an intelligent optimization method known as firefly algorithm (FA) was used by this study to optimize the force tracking controller (FTC) parameters as to achieve the exact damping force of MR damper system. The MR damper was first developed using Spencer model and the required voltage input was then provided by the FTC. The controller parameters were tuned using intelligent FA method in order to find the optimum values which would identify the accuracy of the force tracking that followed the MR damping force. The simulation shows that the FTC with FA technique is able to track the desired force better than the heuristic method up to 1.71 % error considering a given desired input force.

articleTitle: Gameplay Analysis Based on Sequence Model of Popular Game in Play Store
abstract: A Popular game in mobile device have characteristic gameplay feature like pushing, moving or drawing. The understanding of game designer is the main thing to create game which is able to occupy the top free position on the Play Store. One aspect of gaming as software is the interactive feature. When viewed from the sequence diagram model, game being performed by the player is a set of interactions between objects that are viewed based on the life time line of the object. This study aims to find models of interaction between objects such as what supports an interesting gameplay. Data from the position of the bird object towards the pole and floor will be observed. This research uses game Flappy Bird that has been modified using Unity 3D for data recording and validated under all its functions in accordance with the original flappy game. By observing 30 users with good, moderate and bad levels with 40 games per user, player's skill level looks better if the more consistent the number of moves made (number of clicks) and the smaller the amount of excess distance on the x-axis. While the excess distance of movement on the y-axis has more attractive in movement.

articleTitle: EEG–Based Emotion Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Research in recognizing emotion has been done with many methods, one of them by using brain wave or electroencephalography (EEG). The main benefit of using EEG is because of its ability to track events within brain in millisecond accuracy. Psychologist proposed a model to help classify human emotions, which can be divided into four quadrants using two dimensional emotions of arousal and valence. In this paper, Convolutional Neural Network was proposed as a method for recognizing emotion in the EEG data due to its advantages, such as: local connections, shared weights, pooling and using series of layer to handle high dimensional data of EEG. The overfitting problem in EEG dataset arising from insufficient sample data has been successfully addressed using data augmentation process with effective window size of 4 seconds. The best model is achieved with the accuracy of 72% for arousal and 71% for valence.

articleTitle: Upgrading Vibrating Screen for Dewatering–Case Study on Antam Pongkor Gold Processing
abstract: Dewatering is the process of separating a mixture of solids and liquids. Using vibrating screen is one of the possible methods of slurry dewatering with water content of more than 10%. Antam Pongkor has an equipment called Loaded Carbon Vibrating Screen for separating active carbon from slurry. Increasing screen capacity is a must when productions increase. Increasing the capacity of screening can be done by selecting the optimal screen aperture size and using spray water for wet screening. For better dewatering effect, horizontal screen with negative incline is used. After several calculation, analysis, and experimenting, Loaded Carbon Vibrating Screen capacity increase at least 200% with this new configuration compared with previous results.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring in Industrial Area of Orchard Street, Batam City, based on PM2.5 and Carbon Monoxide (CO)
abstract: Orchard street is one of the main streets in Batam City that is often passed by the driver. Pollution in this street not only comes from transport emissions but also from the industrial area. One of the impacts of industrial activity is an increase in air pollution levels in the form of both gas and particulates that have the potential to decrease the ambient air quality. This study was conducted by direct measurement in the field consist of PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> and Carbon Monoxide (CO) gas in every 6 hours with 7 sampling points. Furthermore, the calculated green space was conducted by Google Earth to know about the absorption level of green space. The result showed that the PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</sub> level was less than 45 ug/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, CO level was about 7.67 - 35.83 ppm. For the absorption level of green space in the near study area was 15.6 kg CO/day.

articleTitle: Interactive Indonesia Traditional Fable: Si Kancil
abstract: Reading is an activity to get a message and information that can add insight. However, reading activities in Indonesia especially for children are still low. By utilizing the role of the development of increasingly advanced computer technology, this technology can be utilized to create a new look to present stories to be more interactive and more interestingly packaged in the form of 2D animation. In this interactive story mechanism the user can influence the storyline through actions based on commands chosen against the main characters in a story. The type of story used in this is a popular fable type of fable that is The Mouse Deer.

articleTitle: Design of Stroke Rehabilitation Robots
abstract: One of the most frequent cause of limb disabilities worldwide is stroke. In order to achieve high recoverability, stroke patients require repetitive and consistent rehabilitation treatment. However, the increasing number of stroke patients with limited number of therapists and transportation problem among patients from rural places limit the accessibility to have better treatment. Hence, it is important to have a Rehabilitation Robot Devices (RRDs) to minimize the problems. This research is aimed to design an upper limb rehabilitation robot device that is portable and adjustable. In order to ensure that the robot arm design achieve the desired movement, CATIA V5R22 was used to simulate the design with a human builder. Motion analysis in SolidWork 2018 was used to investigate the angular displacement of the robot arm link. The simulation showed that, the robot arm design corresponds with the Malaysian anthropometry dimensions. The motion analysis showed that, the movement pattern of the robot arm achieved the desired angle of movement during rehabilitation process with the wrist extension recorded the highest time cycle which is 16 seconds for 45 degrees of extension.

articleTitle: Decision Determination of Hinterland Selection Using Analytical Network Process
abstract: Hinterland is an isolated and backward region that still needs attention. Hinterland empowerment that focuses on one place is expected to get more obvious results. Therefore, in its current program, the study center for empowering the islands and borders of Politeknik Negeri Batam will focus its research activities and community services to one of the hinterland in Batam. Batam has 14 hinterland, where each hinterland is considered from 6 criteria (natural resources, education, technology, economy, electricity, transportation) and its sub-criteria. Analytic Network Process (ANP) is used because it is most suitable for getting a choice of hinterland with good resources but lacking in empowerment. In addition, with the ANP method, the relationship between criteria and sub criteria can be known. The results obtained from this study are the selection of one hinterland, namely Temoyong which has the highest priority value, so it is worth recommending to be the object of study. In addition, the best criteria priority is the level of economy and natural resources.

articleTitle: Effect of SiO2 Substrates Condition as Aluminum Nitride Growing Media
abstract: Today's semiconductor technology continues to develop, both in terms of material discovery, manufacturing technique, as well as implementation reduntdant. One of one use consistent terms semiconductor materials that attracts attention is AIN. Several methods have been conducted to grow AIN, one of them is using the reactive sputtering method. This method has several advantages such as simple crystal growing technique, low temperature deposition and easy to control the experiment parameters. In this reserch with a reactive sputtering method on the substrate Si0<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> that has done with variation substrate temperature of (200, 250, 290°C), and the nitrogen gas pressure of 10, 15 and 20 mBar. This study successfully synthesize nanomaterial AlN with a hexagonal crystal s ystem and shows the wurtzite phase is formed. Morphologically, AlN is composed of particles - spherical shaped particles. From this research it is known that raising the temperature of the substrate produces more uniform morphology redundant the surface roughness is formed from 15.4 to 84 nm and the obtained crystal size is 64-87 nm. While the addition of nitrogen gas pressure cause better crystallinity.

articleTitle: Comparison of Strength Between Angular and Elbow Frame Joint on Fiberglass Boats Construction
abstract: The strength of the frame is very important in ship design. in Indonesia there is a principle, the design of frame connections refers to the class rules of the Biro Klasifikasi Indonesia (BKI) or Indonesian Classification Bureau. However, very often there are cracked connections between the side frame and bottom frame on a fiberglass boat. For this reason, it is necessary to analyze and modify the Model of the frame joint so will found a frame joint with better strength. This study investigates modification of the frame joint and analyzing the strength of the connection of the frame with the finite element method (FEM). The final goal is to get a comparison of the stress distributions that occur in all the joint models designed and to compare the stresses. In this study using the main data of boat: the length overall (LOA) is 10.30 meters, breadth (B) is 1.20 meters, height is 0.90 meters and draft (T) is 0.40 meters. the Result is the first model is better than the second model or the joint angular frame model turns out to be better than the elbow frame Joint model which is proven because the stress voltage is smaller is 5.04 MPa while the second model reaches 65 MPa

articleTitle: Face Recognition Based on PCA and Neural Network
abstract: This paper presented a face recognition method based on PCA and Back Propagation Neural Network which is robust and simple algorithm based on image captured by camera. The proposed algorithm is done on three stages, namely face detection, face feature extraction and face recognition. The face detection is performed using Haar-Like Feature. The Haar-Like feature analyzes the pixels in the image into squares by function. The method uses the Adaboost learning algorithm to select a small number of important feature from a large data set. The detected face is then extracted using PCA. PCA will select and reduce the face feature based on eigenvalues of correlation matrix data. We obtain 500 features face extracted using PCA. The face feature becomes the input to neural network for recognition process. The neural network is developed with two hidden layers with 15 nodes on each and three nodes of output layer. The experiment is performed in real time environment. Using 5 faces image data with each data is taken 100 times, the experimental result showed the satisfactory result with 87.5% recognition rate in average.

articleTitle: A New Heart Sound Signal Identification Approach Suitable for Smart Healthcare Systems
abstract: Currently, proliferation of the Internet of Things development has fostered several research efforts and works in smart healthcare systems. One of the important area is the development of automated systems to identify fundamental heart sound signals in the presence of noise and murmur. In this work, we proposed a new scheme for the fundamental heart sound signals identification and murmur by firstly employing the CEEMD algorithm combined with the Pearson distance metric and secondly utilizing the Shannon energy envelope to segment the first fundamental heart sound signal, S1 the second fundamental heart sound signal, S2, and murmur. Here, the CEEMD algorithm and the Pearson distance metric perform signal decomposition to extract murmur from the heart sound signals while the Shannon energy envelope increases the quality of signal features. Based on our evaluation the proposed algorithm showed promising result to identify the S1 and S2 in the presence of murmur. The algorithm at the same time can trace the duration and location of the murmur.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting the Hammer Milling Process of Crude Seawater Salt
abstract: The importance of particle size of common salt, i.e. sodium chloride, has become a concern in many applications; and this is not excluding the salt sourced from solar evaporated seawater. Therefore, milling process to reduce the particle size of the salt is an important part. Hammer milling has an advantage that its open system can lead to higher capacity in one batch. The effects of varying parameters like mill speed and output screen size of hammer milling had been studied in earlier researches. However, the effect of choosing certain heating treatment temperature prior the hammer milling as well as its interaction with either mill speed effect or output screen size effect has not been investigated yet despite the importance of heating treatment of seawater salt. Therefore, this research was conducted to see the effects of heating temperature, mill speed, and output screen size as well as their significance and their interaction in crude seawater salt hammer milling by studying the particle size distribution of the milled samples using sieve analysis. The results showed that heating temperature was the most important factor, especially when rising the temperature from 110 °C to 125 °C, followed by output screen size and mill speed, respectively, in which the effect of changing output screen size as much as 4 times smaller was about 10% higher than the effect of increasing hammer mill speed as much as 2000 rpm. Optimizing the three aforementioned parameters can even produce better milling results than adding further milling (two-times milling).
